<security_assessment>

<details>
This PKGBUILD poses no danger when running `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The file contains only standard packaging metadata at the top level: variable definitions (pkgname, pkgver, pkgrel, arch, url, license, depends, etc.), source URL arrays with version-substituted GitHub release URLs, and sha256sums for both architectures. There are no top-level command substitutions, eval calls, curl|bash patterns, base64-encoded strings, or any other executable code that would run during PKGBUILD sourcing. The `source` arrays reference the package's own upstream GitHub releases, which is normal AUR practice. The `sha256sums` are present (not SKIP), and as explicitly stated in the guidelines, a missing or SKIPped checksum is never grounds to fail this gate. The `package()` function contains only routine `install` commands and a `sed` loop, but since `--printsrcinfo` does not execute `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()`, the function body is out of scope for this gate. No network downloads or data exfiltration occurs during the simple metadata parsing that `--printsrcinfo` performs.
</details>

<details>
This is a standard .SRCINFO metadata file describing the mqvpn-bin AUR package. It contains only declarative package metadata: package name/version, description, upstream URL, architecture support (x86_64 and aarch64), license, dependencies, and source URLs with corresponding SHA256 checksums. The file contains no executable code, scripts, or commands whatsoever — .SRCINFO files are purely declarative and cannot execute anything.

The two download sources point to the project's own official GitHub releases (https://github.com/mp0rta/mqvpn/releases/download/v0.17.0/), which is the expected and standard location for prebuilt binary packages. Both sources have valid SHA256 checksums provided (not SKIP), which is good practice for verifying binary integrity. The options (!strip, !debug) are standard for prebuilt binaries to preserve symbols and debugging information, a common AUR practice.

There are no obfuscated strings, no suspicious network requests to unrelated hosts, no base64/eval patterns, and no unexpected file operations. Everything here is consistent with ordinary packaging of a prebuilt binary application.
</details>

This PKGBUILD appears to be a legitimate Arch Linux package build script. The file downloads a prebuilt binary from the official GitHub releases repository (github.com/mp0rta/mqvpn), provides valid sha256 checksums for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures, and follows standard Arch packaging practices. The package() function installs the binary, a server NAT script (expected for a VPN package), systemd service units (with path substitution from /usr/local to /usr), configuration examples, and license files. There are no eval, base64, curl, or wget commands that execute untrusted code during build. The sed path replacement in the systemd unit loop is a common packaging pattern. No code exfiltrates data, no backdoors or reverse shells are present, and all operations stay within the package's intended scope. The only notable feature is the mqvpn-server-nat.sh script installed to /usr/lib/mqvpn/, but this serves the package's stated VPN functionality and is part of the upstream application, not injected malicious code.
</details>
